paper_title: A 13/6-Approximation for Strip Packing via the Bottom-Left Algorithm
classifications: Theory of computation → Packing and covering problems
statement: In this paper, we presented a new ordering of rectangles under which the Bottom-Left Algorithm achieves an approximation ratio of 13/6, improving the previously best-known bound of 3 for the BL algorithm given by [1]. A key ingredient in our analysis is the detailed study of horizontal lines in the packing and the fraction of each line that is covered by rectangles. For this, we developed a technique based on formulating and solving a quadratic program to determine the number of lines of a given order. This method may also prove useful for refining the analysis of other packing algorithms. Determining the exact approximation ratio of the BL algorithm remains an open and intriguing problem. There are instances for which no ordering of rectangles can achieve a ratio better than 4/3 − ε for the BL algorithm [12], even when all rectangles are squares. Closing the gap between 4/3 − ε and 13/6 is interesting, because of the possibility for the BL algorithm to surpass the current best-known (5/3 + ε)-approximation for Strip Packing [10].
